All the sentences were made to run concurrently.
The trial court though convicted accused No.1 for an offence under Section 506 of the IPC, but did not impose any sentence.
Out of the fine amount, Rs.50,000/- was ordered to be paid to the victim as compensation.
FIR was registered on 14-10-2014.
The prosecution case is that accused No.1 developed friendship with the victim (PW.2), aged 13 years, by giving her chocolates, biscuits etc., and on 13- 10-2014, he introduced her to accused No.2.

On 14-10-2014, accused No.2 picked the victim from Nirman public school after she alighted from the van, contacted accused No.1 over phone and in turn, accused No.1 told the victim to accompany accused No.2 in order to come to his house at Gyanaganganagara,
Bengaluru.
Thus, accused No.2 took the victim to the house of accused No.1 on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-01 EA 6368.
Accused No.1 under threat forcibly committed sexual assault on the Saravanan vs State By Jnanabharathi

on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127956453/
2 victim and in the afternoon, he dropped her back near the school.
The investigation led to filing of charge-sheet for the offences under Sections 366A, 342, 506, 376(1) of the IPC, Section 4 of the POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (POA) Act.

The trial NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB court framed charges for the offences under Sections 366A, 342, 376(1) and 506 of the IPC, Section 4 of the POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (POA) Act against accused No.1 and charges for the offence under Section 363 of the IPC against accused No.2.
3.
The trial court has recorded findings that the evidence of PW.2 is reliable.
She being the victim has narrated the incident in her own words.
Minor discrepancies may be there in her evidence, but they do not go to the root of the prosecution case.
Her evidence clearly discloses as to how she was sexually abused by accused No.1.

The evidence of the victim is corroborated by her father-PW.1,
uncle-PW.4 and the medical evidence of PW.9-doctor, who examined PW.2 and opined that seminal stains were found in her undergarments, her hymen was found torn irregularly, speculum could pass easily and she has NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB undergone act of sexual intercourse.

Therefore, it is the opinion of the trial court that evidence of PW.9 supports the testimony of PW.2.
4.

The trial court opined that accused No.1 by his act of penetrative sexual assault on the victim,
after developing friendship with her, knowing that she belonged to scheduled caste, has spoiled her life and future, deceitfully lured her on the pretext of chocolates, threatened the innocent child victim of 7th standard and committed the aforesaid act.

5. Appreciating the evidence, the conclusion of the trial court is that the offences under Sections 366A, 342, 376(1) and 506 of IPC, Section 4 of the POCSO Act and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (POA) Act are established.
The trial court has also drawn presumption according to Section 29 of the POCSO Act and Section 114A of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.

Assailing the findings of the trial court, the learned counsel for the appellant argued that the trial court committed an error in convicting accused No.1 and would seek to refer to the contradictions in the manner in which the complaint was initiated and the various statements made by the victim herself.

It is contended that the criminal proceeding was set in motion by the complaint (Ex.P.1)
dated 14.10.2014, wherein it has been stated that his daughter was enticed, taken to the house of accused No.1, where he committed sexual act against the victim.
It is his case that even the victim has made contradicting statements with regard to the nature of the incident as also her friendship with accused No.1.

In that light, it is contended that the entire theory of the victim being kidnapped,
enticed or being raped in the manner, as has been put forth, is not reliable.

It is contended that the manner in which the victim had stated of having gone with accused NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB No.2,
it only indicates that it was consensual.
It is contended that the trial court has committed a serious error in holding accused No.1 guilty of the offences when there is serious infirmity in the testimonies of PWs.1, 2 and 4.
PW.2 has clearly admitted that accused No.1 attempted to commit penetrative sexual assault, but the trial court is wrong in brushing aside the entire cross- examination of PW.2

Further, the victim has clearly stated in the cross-examination and before the NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB Magistrate under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. that it was only an attempt to commit rape and not rape.

But the trial court without considering the contents of the statement recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. and cross-examination of the victim, convicted the appellant for the offence under Section 376(1) of the IPC read with Section 4 of POCSO Act, which is against the principles of criminal jurisprudence.

It is contended that accused No.1 was not aware about the fact that the victim and her father belonged to scheduled caste, however, the trial court convicted accused No.1 for the offence under Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (POA) Act.
There is no corroborative evidence in the testimonies of PWs.1, 2 and 4 with regard to enticement of the victim near Nirman Public School and bringing of the victim from the house of accused No.1.
There is nothing on record to show that victim and her father belonged to scheduled caste-chalavadi.

Moreover, the - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB Tahsildar who issued Ex.P.27- caste certificate has not been examined,
but the trial court wrongly held that Ex.P.27 is proved.

Further, the prosecution has not produced any document to prove the age of the victim, in the absence of any such material, the trial court has wrongly held that the victim was minor as on the date of incident.

Further, PW.9-doctor has stated that according to the history given by the victim, accused No.1 was her boyfriend since three years,
no evidence of fresh injuries and there is no bleeding.
Therefore, the evidence is so inconsistent and thereby, the testimony of the victim does not find corroboration neither from PW.1 nor PW.4.

With regard to allegation of sexual assault, clear evidence of PW.9 is that she has not mentioned in Ex.P-17-MLC register entry that after sexual act, the victim washed her private part at the instance of accused No.1 and it ruled out possibility of accused No.1 committing rape on the victim.
There were no - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB injuries near the genital organ and this is another important aspect which makes the testimony of the victim unbelievable.
In view of all these inconsistencies and discrepancies in the evidence, the trial court should not have convicted accused No.1.
Hence, for all these grounds, he prays to allow the appeal.
7. Per contra, Sri Vijayakumar Majage, learned State Public Prosecutor-II, argued that PW2-victim was a minor girl, aged '13' years at the time of incident.
She has fully established the prosecution case.
Her evidence finds corroboration from the medical evidence given by PW.9-the doctor.
PW.9 has stated that hymen was irregular, she has also given evidence that possibly the victim might have been sexually abused.
The fact of the victim being sexually assaulted is proved.
It does not matter even if there is some inconsistency in the evidence in this regard.

It is - 12 - Saravanan vs State By Jnanabharathi on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127956453/
4 NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB not material to shake the entire prosecution case.
PWs.1 and 4 have also given evidence and their evidence cannot be disbelieved.
Since the trial court has properly appreciated the evidence for holding the accused guilty, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
8. We have perused the entire evidence on record and considered the arguments.
The evidence of PW.2-victim shows that she being a girl of tender age gave evidence in her own words.
Her evidence clearly discloses as to how she was enticed by accused No.2 and he dropped her to the house of accused No.1 and what he did by taking her in his house.

She revealed the incident before her father,
uncle and doctor as to how she was enticed by accused No.2 and subjected to sexual assault by accused No.1.
9.

The victim has stated in her examination- in-chief that accused No.1 committed rape, but in - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB her cross-examination and statement before the Magistrate recorded under section 164 of the Cr.P.C., she has stated that accused No.1 attempted to commit rape.
The evidence of PW.9 is that the victim has undergone sexual act.
If the testimony of the victim is again subjected to scrutiny, it appears that she has given a vivid account of the incident.
She has clearly stated as to how accused No.2 enticed her and accused No.1 abused her sexually.
Ex.P15 is the statement given by the girl before the Magistrate under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C.

Even at that time,
she clearly revealed the incident that accused No.1 made an attempt to commit rape.
10. We have taken note of the nature of consideration made by the trial court.

Insofar as the incident based on which the charge was framed against the accused, more particularly against the appellant,
the father and uncle of the - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB victim and the victim herself were examined as PW-1, PW-2 and PW-4,
who have spoken with regard to the same.

Reference was made to the complaint and the statement of PW-1 and at the first instance, the complainant having named appellant, it was in the circumstance when his daughter informed him about the incident i.e., his daughter was taken to the house of accused No.1 and had accordingly lodged the complaint.
It is pursuant to the complaint, the victim gave her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
In that circumstance, what would be relevant is the statement and the evidence tendered by the victim as PW-2 before the trial court.

Though certain discrepancies were referred to by the learned counsel for the appellant in the manner the victim had described the incident to contend that as per her own statement, accused No.1 attempted to commit rape, it is noticed that the sum and substance of the evidence tendered by - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB the victim as PW-2 is essentially with regard to the sexual assault committed by accused No.1.

Saravanan vs State By Jnanabharathi on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127956453/
5 11.

There are minor discrepancies in the statement made under Section 164 Cr.P.C and the evidence tendered by the victim-PW-2, the thrust of the evidence shows that the appellant committed sexual assault on victim.
In such circumstance, the evidence of the victim and the medical evidence would establish the charge of attempt to rape or sexual assault.

12. In order to corroborate oral testimony of victim, PW.9-doctor who examined the victim has stated that victim had undergone sexual act, there were no external injuries all over the body, hymen was torn irregularly, speculum could pass easily, no evidence of fresh injuries, there was no bleeding.

13. In the light of the medical evidence and the testimony of PW-2, the prosecution has been - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB able to prove the ingredient of sections 7 and 8 of POCSO Act, which are as under:
Section 7- Whoever, with sexual intent touches the vagina, penis, anus or breast of the child or makes the child touch the vagina, penis, anus or breast of such person or any other person, or does any other act with sexual intent which involves physical contact without penetration is said to commit sexual assault.

Section 8 - Punishment for sexual assault:
Whoever, commits sexual assault, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than three years but which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine.
14.

The question which would however arise for our consideration is as to "whether the charge framed against the accused under Section 376(1) of IPC would be justified" and as to "whether the case would qualify to be one of penetrative sexual assault or sexual assault".
On - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB this aspect, the evidence of PW-1 and PW-4 does not establish the same.
The evidence of PW-2-the victim is not categorical, inasmuch as, the victim has alleged that when she was in the house of appellant, the appellant committed sexual assault.
In fact, the very conclusion reached by the trial court itself would indicate that the allegation of sexual assault, as established by the prosecution, is against the appellant.
15. In that circumstance, the charge of rape has not been established with convincing evidence.
However, having already noted that the incident of attempt to rape or sexual assault alleged had been established, it would be a case to convict the appellant under Section 8 of POCSO Act.

The conviction imposed by the trial court under Sections 366A and 342 of IPC and the sentence, as Saravanan vs State By Jnanabharathi on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127956453/
6 ordered thereunder, would not call for interference.

On arriving at the conclusion that the appellant is liable to be convicted under Section 8 of the POCSO Act and not under Section 4 of the POCSO Act, the appropriate sentence to be imposed needs consideration.

17. Taking into consideration all the facts including that no material is available on record to indicate that the appellant has any criminal antecedents, it appears that there is no reason to apprehend that the appellant would indulge in similar acts, in future.
In that circumstance, we deem it appropriate to award the sentence of three years and it would be sufficient to serve the ends of justice.

18. Insofar as the charge alleged against the appellant under Section 506 of IPC, it is noticed that the charge alleged against the appellant is that on the date referred to i.e., 14.10.2014, the appellant threatened over phone to kill the victim- - 19 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB the daughter of the complainant and therefore had committed the offence which is punishable under Section 506 of IPC.

In respect of the said charge, we do not find that there is any supporting evidence, except the vague statement of the victim in her evidence as PW-2 that, as soon as, the victim alighted from the school van, accused No.2 came to Nirman public school in order to drop her to the house of accused No.1, at that time, the victim interacted with accused No.1 over phone, thus, accused No.1 insisted her to visit his house, thereby threatened her that he would eliminate her if she failed to visit his house.
There is no other statement or evidence relating to the incident or the manner in which the threat, in its true sense, was put forth.
The evidence of victim is somewhat shaky, as she was in frequent contact with accused No.1 since three years.
In that view, we are of the opinion that the conviction and sentence under Section 506 IPC imposed by the trial court is not - 20 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB sustainable and is liable to be set aside.
19. In order to attract Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (POA) Act is concerned, the prosecution made allegations that the accused persons have committed an offence against the member of Scheduled Caste.
In this regard, they relied upon Ex.P.27 caste certificate issued by Tahsildar.
But the Tahsildar is not examined before the court.

The Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of STATE OF KARNATAKA v. SHARIFSAB @ SHARFANNA in Criminal Appeal No.1522 of 2016 connected with Criminal Appeal No.1530 of 2016 disposed of on 10-03-2023 held that an accused cannot be held Saravanan vs State By Jnanabharathi on 15 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127956453/
7 guilty of offence under Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (POA) Act, by mere production of caste certificate.

sentences.text: Our view is fortified by the dictum of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of HITESH VERMA v. State of UTTARAKHAND AND ANOTHER, reported in - 21 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB (2020) 10 SCC 710.

sentences.text:
Hence, conviction of appellant under section 3(2)(v)
of SC/ST (POA) Act, 1989, is not sustainable in law.
20. In the instant case, the trial court convicted accused No.1 for the offence under section 376(1) of IPC read with section 4 of POCSO Act instead of the offence under section 8 of POCSO Act.
To that extent, the judgment of the trial court requires to be modified.
So far sentences in respect of other offences under sections 366A and 342 of IPC is concerned, it is proper in all respects.

In the result, we pass the following order: -
i.
The appeal is allowed-in-part.

ii. The conviction and sentence passed in S.C.No.57/2015 by learned LXX Additional City Civil and Sessions Judge and Special Judge, Bengaluru City (CCH-71), in - 22 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB respect of offence under Section 506 of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST (POA) Act against accused No.1 is set aside and accused No.1 is acquitted of the above charges;

iv. The order of conviction and sentence passed by the trial court under Section 376(1) of IPC r/w section 4 of POCSO Act is modified.
The appellant is convicted under Section 8 of POCSO Act and is sentenced to undergo simple imprisonment for the period of three years.
The fine and default sentence as imposed by the trial court shall remain unaltered.
v. The accused is entitled to the benefit of set off as contemplated under the - 23 - NC: 2023:KHC:40695-DB provisions of Section 428 of the Code of Criminal Procedure;
vi. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed of.
